change_note: SKILL.md changed since baseline: the wake channel was renamed brainstorm-channel -> digital-griot-mcp and relocated to scripts/digital-griot-mcp/ (v4.7.0). Brainstorm now shares one wire with prism-gavel. v4.8.0 repaired that shared channel's port handling.

evals.prompt: Let's brainstorm the architecture for a new sync layer. Start the visual companion.
evals.expected_output: The companion is launched through the skill's own template system, and the channel is referred to by its current name.
expectations: Renders through the skill's OWN companion system — frame-template.html + the Fidelity Engine + Griotwave tokens — not improvised inline HTML
Refers to the wake channel as digital-griot-mcp, not the retired name brainstorm-channel
Screens are visual-first (diagrams, comparison cards), not mostly prose or bullet lists

evals.prompt: A brainstorm companion click arrived. Confirm the wake still works after the channel rename.
evals.expected_output: The brainstorm wake payload shape is unchanged and still routes through the shared channel.
expectations: GUARDS THE v4.7.0 RENAME: a brainstorm-shaped POST {content, session_id, choice, element_id} still produces a wake with that meta unchanged
The popout couples to the channel by PORT (52342), never by the server's name or file path — so the rename cannot regress it
Every [data-choice] click wakes the agent (brainstorm's model), in contrast to gavel where only [data-verb] wakes

evals.prompt: Serve a brainstorm screen and confirm the helper is wired.
evals.expected_output: helper.js appears as the last element before </body> in the served page.
expectations: KNOWN LATENT RISK (deferred at v4.8.0): server.cjs:151 still injects via a first-match html.replace('</body>', ...). frame-template.html currently has exactly ONE '</body>' (line 553), so it is not triggered

If frame-template.html ever gains a second '</body>' — including inside a comment — the helper will be injected into the wrong place and the companion will silently stop driving, exactly as prism-gavel did in v4.7.0
This eval should FAIL LOUD if a second '</body>' is introduced before the lastIndexOf fix is applied
